::: {.resource-intro}
**The essential idea:** A reference manager such as Zotero stores bibliographic records and can connect them to PDFs, notes, and drafts. It does not replace careful reading or citation verification.
:::

## Core practices

### Capture the record

Save a source with its DOI or stable URL and check author names, title, publication, date, and source type.

### Organize for retrieval

Use collections for projects and a small, consistent set of tags for themes or reading status.

### Cite carefully

Use your word processor’s citation integration, then verify that the output matches the required style and the underlying source.

## A simple workflow

Create a project collection; import one source from a scholarly database and another from a DOI; inspect both metadata records; attach or link the full text where permitted; add a note on why each source matters.

## In context

::: {.callout-example}
A collaborative coastal monitoring project uses one shared collection for approved references and personal notes for interpretation, reducing duplicate downloads without conflating different researchers’ conclusions.
:::

## Keep in mind

Back up or sync your library appropriately and respect copyright and access conditions when sharing PDFs.
